proposals.before: Together with Xing Shao of Hejian and Wang Xin of Beihai, he all supported their aged mothers and took wives and children on the same journey to Qing and Qi.
proposals.after: Together with Xing Shao of Hejian and Wang Xin of Beihai, they each supported their aged mothers and took wives and children on the same journey to Qing and Qi.
proposals.reason: Literal English uses ungrammatical singular 'he all supported' for a plural joint subject; Chinese 俱 marks that all three did so.

proposals.before: His father Zun was staff officer of the Eastern Campaigning Headquarters in Jizhou under Wei; when Prince Jingzhao Yu of Jingzhao rose in revolt in Jizhou, he met disaster and was killed.
proposals.after: His father Zun was staff officer of the Eastern Campaigning Headquarters in Jizhou under Wei; when Prince Jingzhao Yu rose in revolt in Jizhou, he met disaster and was killed.
proposals.reason: Literal redundantly repeats 'of Jingzhao' after the title Prince Jingzhao; Chinese has 京兆王愉 once.

proposals.before: At age six he himself wished to enter school; his family, observing a taboo of the year by chance, made an appointment and would not allow it.
proposals.after: At age six he himself wished to enter school; his family, by chance observing a taboo of the year, restrained him and would not allow it.
proposals.reason: 約而弗許 means they bound/forbade him, not that they 'made an appointment'.

proposals.before: At the time an edict had the attendant-in-ordinary Prince Xihe of the Western River, Secretary Director Chang Jing, and ten Confucian scholars compile the Five Rites; Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan together took charge of military rites.
proposals.after: At the time an edict had the attendant-in-ordinary Prince of Xihe, Secretary Director Chang Jing, select ten Confucian scholars to compile the Five Rites; Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan together took charge of military rites.
proposals.reason: 'Prince Xihe of the Western River' double-renders 西河; also 選儒學十人 means they were to select ten scholars.

proposals.before: At the time Gao Cheng had Xian select the chief clerk of the ministry of rites; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end it did not come to pass — all said it was because of this letter.
proposals.after: At the time Gao Cheng had Xian select the chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end it did not come to pass — all said it was because of this letter.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is the Minister over the Masses, not the ministry of rites (禮部/太常).

decisions.reason: Chinese names him once as 京兆王愉; 'Prince Jingzhao Yu of Jingzhao' doubles the fief already in the title, so dropping the redundant 'of Jingzhao' matches the source.
約而弗許 means the family constrained/forbade him; 'made an appointment' is a modern false friend of 約 and is not supported by the Chinese.
The same 約而弗許 in the literal field is restraint and refusal, not arranging a meeting; 'restrained him and would not allow it' is accurate.

decisions.after: At the time an edict had the attendant-in-ordinary Prince of Xihe and Secretary Director Chang Jing select ten Confucian scholars to compile the Five Rites; Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan together took charge of military rites.
decisions.reason: The proposal rightly drops the double rendering of 西河 and restores 選 before 儒學十人, but the comma list before 'select' is awkward; join the two officials with 'and' so the causative reads cleanly.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 侍中西河王、秘書監常景選儒學十人緝撰五禮

decisions.reason: 司徒長史 is the chief clerkship under the Situ (Minister over the Masses), not an office of the ministry of rites; the replacement corrects that office title.
Literal 司徒長史 likewise belongs to the Minister over the Masses; 'ministry of rites' invents a different bureau not in the Chinese.
司徒右長史 is right chief clerk of the Situ; rendering it as of the ministry of rites misidentifies the office, and the proposed wording restores the correct affiliation.
The literal field has the same 司徒右長史 error; 'Minister over the Masses' matches the Chinese office title.
